clue.text: Total a couple of graduates retains is capital

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the opening letters hold the next word inside them

blocks.note: to total is to add up
taken as written
taken as written
BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, and a couple means two of them

explanation.surface: An accountant adds up two graduates' earnings and finds the total includes something.
explanation.walkthrough: The subject of 'retains' is the whole phrase before it, so the word is sits inside that chain rather than around any one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia, so the answer is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Delighted to see PR about model

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word wraps around the next

blocks.note: public relations work promotes things, as an advertisement does
an artist's model is their muse, the person who inspires them

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that a publicity team has taken up a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: PR usually means public relations; here it stands for an advertisement, the short form of which is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Being amused means being entertained and pleased, a close synonym of delighted.

clue.text: Receipt from pendant initially ten times as valuable

indicators.note: the first letter, read as a Roman numeral, is swapped for the numeral worth ten times as much

blocks.note: a locket is a pendant worn on a chain

explanation.surface: A jeweller's receipt shows a pendant was sold for ten times its value.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the Roman numeral 50; ten times that is 500, which is D, so LOCKET becomes DOCKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A docket is a document listing goods delivered or paid for, which serves as a receipt.

clue.text: Variable amounts of trombone practice?

blocks.note: first meaning: a scale of fees or charges that changes with circumstances
second meaning, playful: a trombonist slides the instrument while running up and down a scale

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, whimsical sense: a trombone changes pitch by its slide, so practising scales means sliding through them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding scale is a system of payments that varies with income or conditions, hence variable amounts.

clue.text: Hiccup taking first taste of brown sauce

indicators.note: a first taste is just the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of brown
sauce is cheeky talk, as is lip

explanation.surface: A cook stumbles while sampling some brown sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown sauce' looks like one item from the kitchen; the sauce here is cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a minor temporary setback or glitch, and a hiccup is used in the same figurative way.

clue.text: Book every defective vehicle

blocks.note: B is a standard abbreviation for book
every and each are synonyms
software full of faults is buggy

explanation.surface: Someone wants every faulty car brought in or reported.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach buggy is a small open motor car built for driving on sand, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Where fortune’s shown growth in the tropics

blocks.note: first meaning: palmists read your future from the lines on your hand
second meaning: a tree that flourishes in hot climates

explanation.walkthrough: Fortune suggests wealth, but here it is the future a fortune-teller reads.
explanation.definitionFit: The inside of the hand is read in palmistry, and the same word names a tropical tree with large fronds.

clue.text: Pirate’s rum providing something to drink

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the preceding word is turned into an odd arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
providing that means if

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's rum ration provides something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the pirate's drink, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: One gets taken out and put into a home

definitions.text: One gets taken out and put into a home

blocks.clueFragment: One gets taken out and put into a home
blocks.note: surface reading: an old or ill person is removed and placed in a care home
setter's reading: a loan is taken out, and the money is put into buying a house

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken out' and 'put into a home' suggest a person moved into residential care; in fact it is a loan taken out and invested in property.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a loan secured on a property, taken out by a buyer to purchase a house.

clue.text: Body in NY on life support, letting things go

blocks.note: the United Nations is an organisation headquartered in New York
a patient on life support is in a critical condition

explanation.surface: A body in a New York hospital is kept alive on life support, until the plug is pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: Body suggests a corpse or patient; it is an international organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncritical person does not find fault, accepting or overlooking things rather than challenging them.

clue.text: Disciple’s heartless gaze

blocks.note: Peter was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus

explanation.surface: A follower stares coldly, without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER loses its middle letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely or searchingly, a kind of gazing.

clue.text: Travelling supporter that needs to be taken in hand

definitions.text: that needs to be taken in hand

blocks.note: first meaning: a prop that holds you up as you go about on foot

blocks.clueFragment: that needs to be taken in hand
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: a thing you must hold in your grip to use

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an unruly away fan who must be brought under control; both halves literally describe the same aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking stick is a cane carried by hand to support someone while they walk.

clue.text: Twisting in grip of crocodile, yelling ‘It’s snapped shut!’

indicators.note: held in the grip of the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them
twisting round turns the run of letters to face the other way

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of crocodile and the start of yelling

explanation.surface: Someone screams as a crocodile rolls them in its jaws, which slam shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters DILEYE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelid is the fold of skin that closes over the eye, so it is something that snaps shut in a blink.

clue.text: Miserably sparing about hotel passage’s construction

indicators.note: done miserably means done badly, so the next word's letters come out in a poor order
about means around, so the rearranged letters go around the next item

blocks.note: the letters of sparing rearranged
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A stingy guest grumbles about the corridor being built in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside after the P: P(H)RASING.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasing is the way words are put together, which is how a written or musical passage is constructed.

clue.text: Writing style roughly used in comic strip

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the following word is jumbled about
used inside, so the preceding item goes within the jumbled letters

blocks.note: a type is a kind or style
the letters of strip rearranged
C stands for circa, Latin for about or roughly

explanation.surface: A cartoon strip uses a roughly drawn lettering style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic strip' reads as one thing, but comic is the jumble signal for strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Typescript is text produced on a typewriter, so it is a form of writing.

clue.text: One that’s down now, with a high-flying future?

definitions.text: One that’s down now, with a high-flying future?

blocks.clueFragment: One that’s down now, with a high-flying future?

setter's reading: down is the soft fluff of a young bird, one that will later soar as a swan

explanation.walkthrough: Down sounds like low spirits; it is the fluffy plumage of a chick. In Hans Christian Andersen's tale the despised chick grows into a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a plain or unpromising youngster who later becomes beautiful or successful, from the fairy tale.

clue.text: Repacked case and so on to go up in rocket

indicators.note: packing something again puts its contents back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
et al is the Latin abbreviation meaning and others

explanation.surface: Someone repacks a suitcase and other things before setting off in a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to increase rapidly, as prices or costs rocket upward.

clue.text: Silence about north country criminal world

blocks.note: to gag someone is to silence them

a land is a country

explanation.surface: Organised crime keeps a northern region quiet through intimidation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North country' reads as one phrase, the north of England, but the two words supply separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangland is the realm of organised crime and the gangs that run it, the criminal underworld.

clue.text: Surfer uses this gear seen in waves, worn by companion

something worn sits on the wearer, so the jumbled letters enclose the next item

blocks.note: the letters of these words rearranged
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A surfer in the waves wears gear, with a friend alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfer is someone browsing the internet, not riding the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet surfer looks things up on the web through a tool such as Google, hence the answer.

clue.text: Trek one’s taken round service area to get lift

A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.walkthrough: Service area suggests a motorway stop; it is two separate pieces.

clue.text: Claim member’s overcome by booze

explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to state something is true without proof, which is to claim it.

clue.text: Some American gel I candied for decoration

definitions.text: Some American gel I candied for decoration

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a stretch of their letters

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of American to the start of candied

explanation.walkthrough: The definition overlaps the hidden letters, sharing the word candied.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica stalks are crystallised in sugar and used as green decoration on cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom of Italy — old king’s making comeback

blocks.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
Lear is the legendary ancient king of Shakespeare's play, plus the apostrophe s

explanation.definitionFit: Israel was a kingdom of the Hebrew Bible era, the northern realm of the Israelites.

clue.text: Famous site of raga’s composition?

explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the Indian city home to the Taj Mahal, one of the world's most famous monuments.

clue.text: Unhappily having starter of spinach

the opening letter of spinach

an age is a period of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over border' reads as crossing a frontier; it is the signal to turn the border word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a long journey to a holy place, so it is a kind of journey.

clue.text: Finishes relay on a cycle

explanation.definitionFit: Ends as a verb means concludes or stops, so it matches finishes in the third person.
